design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (pro_credit_account_servicing, category trade). Resumed session: on resume the difficulty directory was empty; everything below was authored and persisted in this session, piece by piece (extended.yaml policy by policy, task_tools.py, then this task section by section), with the per-task gates run as soon as each piece existed.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"key": "env_0046_home_improvement_retailer/pro_credit_account_servicing/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6, 6]}. Assignment: trade_ext_credit_line_sizing 6, trade_ext_statement_late_charge 6, trade_ext_dispute_settlement_credit 6, trade_ext_phone_payoff 5. Task 1 draw ({prerequisite_problems: 1, factor_counts: [4, 5]}) was printed at the same time for the headroom check.

[Why a good test] The customer asks for one thing: her submitted line increase decided today. The new line (162500.00) is reachable only after (a) reading from the line rule that the decision waits on a payment after the latest statement covering its past-due amount, (b) the customer choosing to pay the account off, whose figure (101840.27) waits on two state-form prerequisites the agent must discover in the records: the 2026-09 statement shows 58014.73 past due with no late payment charge against it, and the approved dispute on INV-1846-605290 has no credit. Each of the four writes is a 5-6 factor computation over ledger history and the ProBuild Rewards membership (another difficulty's product). Difficulty is in reading the policies, querying the records and calculating; every tool is distinct and atomic.

[Scope] Occupied before: nothing (first task). Claimed: trade_ext_credit_line_sizing (root, trade_credit_limit_changed), trade_ext_phone_payoff (trade_payment_received, owner=user), trade_ext_statement_late_charge (trade_fee_assessed late_payment_charge), trade_ext_dispute_settlement_credit (trade_dispute_credit_posted); tools decide_credit_line_increase_746194e9, submit_payoff_payment_22b2623b, assess_late_payment_charge_c9e93ff5, post_dispute_credit_3cc5c337. Left for task 1 (one prerequisite problem, factors 4 and 5): courtesy waivers (trade_fee_waived), fee corrections (trade_fee_reversed), tax credits, return credits, prompt-payment discounts, settings and closure, and payments on revolving accounts - a full independent tree remains.

[Problem tree card] root trade_ext_credit_line_sizing.
 Edge 1 root -> trade_ext_phone_payoff: state_gate, gate trade_transactions.amount, form state, sentence 'A new credit line is not decided until the ledger shows a payment credited after the latest statement date that at least equals that statement's past-due amount.' (negated direction; the line desk states it as 'not decided until'). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; record-visible state (a payment line dated after the statement); no tool/id/code token; exact scope (any payment covering that past-due amount). The only write of this difficulty that creates a payment line is the payoff policy's tool (owner=user). False at opening: statement 4ad3fef4 past_due_amount 58014.73 dated 2026-09-30; newest payment line dated 2026-07-30. Flips when step 13 credits 101840.27 on 2026-10-07.
 Edge 2 payoff -> trade_ext_statement_late_charge: value_input, gate fees, form state, sentence 'The payoff figure is fixed only after the latest closed statement, when it shows more days past due than the tier's late charge grace days, carries a late payment charge on the ledger.' (affirmative). Only the late charge policy's write books a late payment charge, and that policy charges exactly the latest closed statement beyond the grace days. False at opening: the 2026-09 statement shows 19 days past due (> 5) and no charge carries 2026-09; late charges exist only for 2025-09 (4131fed1) and 2025-12 (99493e91). True on the gold terminal world after step 11. Effect: fees +172.94 and the 12-month late-charge count 1 -> 2 (repeat-lateness loading 0 -> 0.25).
 Edge 3 payoff -> trade_ext_dispute_settlement_credit: value_input, gate dispute_credits, form state, sentence 'The payoff figure is not fixed until every invoice dispute standing approved on the account has its dispute credit on the ledger.' (negated). Only the dispute credit policy's write books a dispute credit. False at opening: request bf78b495 approved 2026-10-05, no dispute credit line. Effect: dispute credits 0 -> 2383.28.
 Derivation (sentence + records + depended-on rule -> action): the line rule names a payment after the statement; the payoff rule is the policy whose write is a payment. The payoff rule names a missing late charge and a missing dispute credit; the late charge rule books 'a late payment charge ... assessed against that statement row', the dispute rule books 'one dispute credit against the disputed invoice'. Topological order: dispute credit, late charge, payoff, line. The two parallel prerequisites commute (neither computation reads the other's write; swapped replay gives the identical terminal hash: True). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip step 9 -> payoff 104223.55 (gold 101840.27); skip step 11 -> payoff 101659.65 and line 173000.00 (gold 162500.00); skip step 13 -> the line may not be decided at all (state gate), terminal lacks the payment line. user_scenario never names a statement, charge or dispute; the tools check nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] trade_credit_limit_changed: trade_credit_line_increase gates active_account (status active), tenure (opened 2019-06-17, Net 45 requires 12 months; boundary 2020-06-17 inclusive), cooldown (changed 2025-03-10, 12 months; boundary 2026-03-10 inclusive); trade_agg_relationship has no gate (one account, 120000.00 vs cap 1250000.00). Requested 175000.00 is below the Net 45 financials threshold 250000.00, so Customer Care decides. trade_payment_received: payable_status (active); debit_authorized is retired by the payoff overwrite and replaced by 'authorized and submitted by the business itself' (the customer runs the tool and states 'You say plainly that you authorize that debit.'). trade_fee_assessed: trade_evt_late_charges.one_per_period (no late charge for 2026-09 yet); trade_evt_payment_application and trade_evt_returned_payment govern the same event with no applicable gate (policy_scope). trade_dispute_credit_posted: filed_in_window (invoice 2026-08-04, filed 2026-09-02 = day 29 of 60), dispute_approved (retired by the overwrite of 'it credits the disputed amount ...' and restated in the rule 'a dispute credit posts only when the invoice dispute request has status approved'), one_dispute_credit (none posted).

[Factor card - trade_ext_statement_late_charge = 172.94, all-baseline 870.22] standing reduction (parameter, cross pro, multi-source): Gold and one other late charge in 12 months (2025-12-31; near-miss 2025-09-30 is 12 whole months back and excluded) -> 0.50 (-> 305.98). volume reduction (parameter, cross pro): net 12-month ProBuild spend 394170.00 (the 38600.00 line of 2025-09-22 is outside) and 87 months -> 0.10 (-> 199.55). dispute relief (parameter): the 2026-09-02 dispute was open on 2026-09-30, Gold -> 0.25 (-> 239.46). small-balance allowance (parameter): no returned payment and 15 payment lines in 24 months -> 1000.00 (-> 175.98). month share (method): 19 days past due on Net 45 -> days counted / 30 (baseline full month -> 370.60). days counted (method, cross pro): enrolled 125 months with a dedicated rep -> 19 - 5 = 14 (-> 234.71). 57014.73 x 0.65/100 x 14/30 = 172.94.
[Factor card - trade_ext_phone_payoff = 101840.27, all-baseline 102035.64] regular-payer reduction 0.50 (14 payment lines, guarantee; -> 101859.35); repeat-lateness loading 0.25 (2 late charges after step 11, 19 dpd; -> 101832.59); accrual start (method) after grace: 2 days (-> 101959.48); day count (method) actual/365 for Net 45 / Net 60 Enterprise, half-month periods for Net 30 Select, actual/360 for Net 30 (the live fall-through and baseline) (-> 101840.94); payoff tolerance 40.00 (rep, spend >= 100000; -> 101880.27). Ledger 101832.59 + accrual 7.68.
[Factor card - trade_ext_credit_line_sizing = 162500.00, all-baseline 144000.00] increase percentage (parameter, cross pro, multi-source) 30 (-> 150000.00); late-charge share 0.80 (one charge in window; -> 173000.00); count window (parameter: lookback length, cross pro) 6 months (baseline 12 months counts 2 -> 146500.00); seasoning 5 points (-> 156000.00); guarantee treatment (method: multiply the core increase by 1.10 / add a flat 2500.00 / leave it) on the multiply tier (-> 158500.00); usage multiplier 1.15 (peak 127283.63 on 2026-03-31 above the line; -> 156500.00).
Every factor sits off its fall-through; no stamp field decides any tier (tiers come from counts, dates, the ledger and the ProBuild records).

user_scenario: You are Renata Okafor-Lindqvist, owner and principal of Copperline Restoration Group LLC, a Chicago remodeling outfit that runs its materials through a Ridgeline Commercial Account Net 45. You are calling from the truck between job sites, brisk and friendly, used to getting straight answers. Open by saying that on Monday you put in a request through the pro desk to raise the credit line on your Net 45 account to $175,000, because the Halsted Street rehab is about to take a big lumber and drywall package, and you want it decided today while you are on the phone. You are asking for the line to be raised now, not just for a quote. You give your details only when the agent asks for them: the phone number on the profile is 7735550231 and the last four of the company EIN are 3187; if asked for the business name it is Copperline Restoration Group LLC; if a ZIP code is wanted, the billing ZIP is 60618. You do not know any account or reference numbers by heart and you tell the agent to look them up. If the agent asks whether you are authorized, you say you are the owner and principal and the line request was yours. If the new line the agent can approve comes out lower than $175,000, you say that is fine and to set it at whatever they can approve today; you never name a different number yourself. If the agent mentions overdue invoices, you say you know a couple ran past their due date over the summer. Only if the agent tells you that a payment has to be made before the line can be decided, you say you would rather settle the whole account at once: you want to pay the account off in full today by phone from the business checking account you always pay from, and you ask the agent for the payoff figure. You say plainly that you authorize that debit. When the agent hands the payment over to you to submit, you submit it yourself for exactly the payoff figure the agent gave you and read back the confirmation you get. If the agent says other entries have to be posted to the account first, you tell them to go ahead with whatever has to be booked; you do not ask what they are and you do not question the amounts. You do not volunteer anything about statements, charges or disputes, and if the agent asks you to confirm a figure on the account you say you do not have the statement in front of you and the system figure is what counts. Once the agent tells you the new credit line has been approved and set, you thank them, say you will let the Halsted crew know, and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The payoff has two parallel prerequisites, the dispute credit (step 9) and the late payment charge (step 11). Neither computation reads what the other writes: the dispute credit reads the approved request, the disputed invoice line, the account age and the ProBuild membership; the late charge reads the latest statement, the late-charge and returned-payment counts, the payment-line count, the most recent dispute request's dates and the membership. The recompute with either write skipped leaves the other unchanged (2383.28 and 172.94), the two rows have argument-derived ids, and each tool moves the cached balance by its own amount, so replaying the gold with steps 8-9 and 10-11 swapped gives the identical terminal DB hash (checked: True). The payoff and the line decision come after both and are fixed by the edges.
